SearchAliases: A paired danger-ground image for entering, dwelling in, or ranging freely through places that would ordinarily threaten or bind a participant
Senses.Note: The two perilous locations intensify one another without becoming a ritual cosmology. No lamp is retained.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X70/X70n1391.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Xiyan Liaohui. Occurrences.Kwic: 師拈拄杖云：祇這箇，本來無形段，醜貌百千般，特地為拈出，牛頭尾上安。有人提得去，促無量劫為一剎那，延一剎那為無量劫，魔宮虎穴任意安居，酒肆婬坊隨緣放曠
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X72/X72n1439.xml). Incense-Offering Record of Chan Master Weilin Daopei. Weilin Daopei owns the retained deployment: at the birthday fund sermon he raises his staff - this thing with no fixed shape, a bull's head set on a tail - and says whoever lifts it away compresses endless kalpas into a thought, and in demon palace and tiger's den dwells at will, roaming free through taverns and brothels by conditions.

Senses.Explanation: Demon palace and tiger cave jointly name dangerous ground entered without avoidance. Yuanwu Keqin uses the expression through Yuanwu's direct statement that patch-robed monks can dwell even there. Zhulangsheng independently deploys it through independent Linji-style ranging through the paired danger grounds.
